reason: Both methods perform identical byte‑to‑long conversion: they read eight consecutive bytes from the supplied array starting at the given index, mask each byte with 0xFF, shift it by multiples of eight, and OR the results into a long. For any valid input (array length ≥ index+8) they produce the same value. For invalid inputs (array too short or null) both throw the same exception type (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException or NullPointerException). No deterministic, bounded input can cause one method to return a different value, throw a different exception, or terminate differently than the other.
